midWorkAdversarialCheck.question: Is there any way the B verdict from CP1 is wrong -- e.g. is 134,600ish itself a ceiling imposed by something all three drops share (a shared upstream bug at Hays CAD's export system, or a filter our own counting script silently applies)?
checksRun: The standalone recount script (count_orion_property.mjs) contains no property-type or use-code filter -- verified by reading it back after writing it; it iterates every data row and only skips on a blank PropertyID, matching lib/cad-ingest/src/orion/parser.ts's own loop exactly.

The Certified export's PropertyTypeCode breakdown (R=123429, P=8682, M=2479, N=10, summing to the full 134600) shows all four property classes present in roughly the proportions expected for a Texas county (residential dominant, some personal/mobile-home) -- not a single class cut off, which would be the signature of a category-level export bug.

The three counts come from three DIFFERENT files, fetched at three different times (2026-03, 2026-07, 2026-08), through two different export code paths on Hays CAD's own systems (the informal PropertyDataExport CSV convention vs. their own 'Orion Certified Export' naming). A bug shared by all three would have to live on Hays CAD's appraisal-roll side itself, at which point it stops being an 'acquisition' question and becomes exactly the operator-ruling case the dispatch names for mechanism B ('the county needs an operator ruling about serving a county whose own appraisal district has not published a complete current roll').
midWorkAdversarialCheck.conclusion: No basis found to overturn CP1's B verdict. Not proceeding to re-acquire.
